extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers, veterans, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: A multi-topic newspaper article summarizing government actions and policy changes at the end of WWII (atomic-energy proposals, veterans' benefits, military reorganizations, surplus disposal, etc.). Intended to inform the general public and interested stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Steps proposed for international atomic-energy commission
rubrics_metrics.description: Four-step agenda laid out in the Moscow communiqué for a proposed commission: (1) Exchange of basic scientific information between nations; (2) Control of atomic energy to insure its use for peaceful purposes; (3) Elimination of atomic and other weapons capable of mass destruction; (4) Erection of effective safeguards by way of inspection and other means to protect complying states against hazards of violations and evasions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commission would be set up by the United Nations and be accountable to the world Security Council. The four objectives were intended to be read together and accompanied by full security requirements, and the plan would be finally subject to congressional approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cautious, step-by-step disclosure of atomic secrets
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. policy described as favoring a cautious, step-by-step disclosure of atomic-energy information rather than immediate full divulgence of technical details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed practice: test proposed inspection methods first and avoid revealing full technical details of the atomic bomb to nations other than Britain and Canada until inspection methods have been demonstrated workable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission accountability and security requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any international atomic-energy commission should be accountable to the UN Security Council and operate under 'full security requirements.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senators and administration officials emphasized that security safeguards and congressional oversight/approval must accompany any international control arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ten-man joint Army-Navy advisory board composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Creation of a ten-man joint Army-Navy advisory board to work with the military director of the atomic-bomb project, with equal representation for each service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board membership indicates study of all possible military uses (including strategic and tactical uses) and coordination among services; equal service representation was stressed as a principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the joint advisory board's study (atomic-bomb uses)
rubrics_metrics.description: The advisory board was to study all possible uses of the bomb in warfare, including forthcoming warship tests and potential tactical applications against troops or fortified positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although specific test dates were not fixed, the membership suggested broad review (aviation, naval, ground forces perspectives) and special attention to assembling personnel, ships, aircraft and technical equipment for tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Navy surplus disposal procedure and priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Navy declared $56,000,000 of building materials and 5,000 Quonset huts surplus and established procedures for disposal through the Reconstruction Finance Corporation (RFC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government agencies (including the Veterans Administration) have top priority for used barrack-type dwellings; disposal teams from the RFC working with naval personnel will conduct spot clean-up sales; the procedure is intended as a pattern for a national program at other depots. Quonset huts are convertible to family housing and may be adapted for different climates.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Department procedure for postponing publication in response to protest
rubrics_metrics.description: The State Department postponed the release of a MacMahon booklet after Reuters protested alleged false statements about Reuters' activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The department delayed release to give Reuters time to prepare documentary refutation and promised to release simultaneously any statement submitted by Reuters to the Department; action taken in response to libel allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: House Banking Committee scrutiny of proposed British loan
rubrics_metrics.description: The Banking Committee planned thorough study and public hearings on the proposed $4,400,000,000 British credit; members insisted on long study and full hearings before a vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee will examine whether objectives will be attained, whether the loan is a good business deal, and what contributions it would make to world trade; input from farm and labor organizations and full public transparency were indicated as expected parts of the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coast Guard transfer and peacetime role guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive order transferring the Coast Guard back to the Treasury Department for peacetime functions effective Jan. 1, with some ships and personnel possibly remaining with the Navy temporarily to assist demobilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In peacetime the Coast Guard should concentrate on standard duties (watching coasts, helping ships in trouble, spotting icebergs, maintaining navigation aids). It was directed to retain air-sea rescue work and maintenance of air-sea navigational aids and mid-ocean weather stations for a mutually agreed period.

rubrics_metrics.name: GI Bill — timing to start and complete education or training
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments extend the period during which a course may be started and lengthen the time allowed to complete training: a veteran may start up to four years after discharge, and the time limit for completing courses increased from seven to nine years after the end of the war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These extensions give veterans greater flexibility in beginning and completing educational and training programs; specific eligibility timing rules should be checked with the Veterans Administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: GI Bill — age and service-based entitlement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: No age limit to qualify for education or training benefits; any eligible veteran may receive one year of education or training plus an additional year for each year of active military service. A veteran need not have been under 25 when he entered service nor show that his education was interrupted by war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple courses may be taken in one year; entitlement and course-cost limits are tied to years of service (see cost caps).

rubrics_metrics.name: GI Bill — correspondence course payment and eligibility charging
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government will pay the cost of a correspondence course (total amount payable $500), but no subsistence is payable while taking correspondence courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A correspondence course counts against the veteran's period of eligibility, with the text indicating a one-fourth charging rule against eligibility (veterans should confirm exact charging rules with VA).

rubrics_metrics.name: GI Bill — increased subsistence allowance rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Amended bill increases subsistence allowances for schooling: single men from $50 to $65 per month; married men from $75 to $90 per month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These new rates apply to schooling benefits; separate vocational rehabilitation rates for disabled veterans are higher (see vocational rehabilitation entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: GI Bill — vocational rehabilitation allowances for disabled veterans
rubrics_metrics.description: Disabled veterans in vocational rehabilitation receive a minimum of $105 per month if without dependents; $115 with a dependent plus $10 for the first child, $7 for each additional child, and $15 for a dependent parent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a veteran receives a lesser pension he will receive these higher amounts while in training; in no event will his pension be reduced when he enters training. Vocational training time limits were also extended (see timing entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: GI Bill — real estate and business loan guarantees
rubrics_metrics.description: Government will guarantee a real-estate loan up to $4,000 (previously $2,000), guaranteeing up to 50% of the total loan subject to the $4,000 cap. Business-loan guarantee limit remains at $2,000 or 50%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For loan purposes the appraisal phrase changed from 'reasonable normal value' to 'reasonable value' and the appraisal must be acceptable to the lender, the veteran, and a VA-designated appraiser.

rubrics_metrics.name: GI Bill — repeal of deduction of benefits from future bonus
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory provision that any financial benefits received under the GI Bill would be deducted from any future bonus was repealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Veterans' GI benefits will not be offset against prospective bonus payments under the amended law.
